standards.title: Cell cycle, mitosis, and cancer
standards.description: Students describe the cell cycle and its checkpoints, explain how mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells, and explain cancer as a loss of cell-cycle control.
history: Merges the former B7.1 Cell Cycle and Its Control, former B7.2 Mitosis, and former B7.3 Cancer. Cancer becomes exam content and a standing Wonder Period topic rather than its own standard.

exam.examItems: MC Q1, Q2; SA 11, 12; Part 4 Diagram

standards.title: Meiosis and genetic variation
standards.description: Students explain how meiosis produces haploid gametes and creates genetic variation.
history: Unchanged from the former B7.4 Meiosis. Absorbs the former B7.5 Genetic Variation from Meiosis.

exam.examItems: MC Q3, Q4; SA 13, 14; Part 3 CER

standards.title: Mendelian genetics: segregation and independent assortment
standards.titleAsPrinted: Mendelian Genetics: Segregation and Independent Assortment
standards.description: Students predict offspring from single-gene and two-gene crosses.
history: Merges the former B9.1 Mendel's Laws and former B9.2 Dihybrid Crosses and Probability. This standard is no longer the unit's keystone; that status now belongs to B7.2 Meiosis, the mechanism that explains it.

standards.title: Beyond Mendel: incomplete dominance, codominance, multiple alleles, and sex linkage
standards.titleAsPrinted: Beyond Mendel: Incomplete Dominance, Codominance, Multiple Alleles, and Sex Linkage
standards.description: Students explain inheritance patterns that are not simple dominant and recessive, and connect inheritance to the behavior of chromosomes carrying more than one gene.
history: From the former B9.3 Beyond Mendel. Absorbs the chromosome-theory, sex-linkage, and gene-linkage content from the former B9.5 The Chromosomal Basis: Sex Linkage and Linked Genes. The nondisjunction and karyotype content from that same former standard goes to B7.5 instead; see that standard for the split.

standards.title: Chromosomal disorders and pedigrees
standards.description: Students analyze human inheritance using pedigrees and explain how errors in meiosis produce chromosomal disorders.
history: Unchanged from the former B9.4 Human Inheritance and Pedigrees. Absorbs the nondisjunction and karyotype content from the former B9.5 The Chromosomal Basis: Sex Linkage and Linked Genes; the linkage and sex-linkage content from that same former standard goes to B7.4 instead, not here.
